Thanks — putting together the tech pieces. Draft notes below (I'll attach formal runbook PDF + two snippet files).

1) What Redwood delivers (private deployments):
- Continuous syslog export (RFC5424) to customer-managed collector or a recommended forwarder in the VPC (we support direct Splunk HEC and UDP/TCP syslog gateways).
- HEC: we recommend a dedicated HEC token per customer with short-lived rotation; TLS mutual auth for private links where possible.
- OTLP traces: runtime emits OpenTelemetry spans to a local OTEL collector sidecar (recommended) or a remote endpoint; we supply tracehook snippets and example span attributes to include/error codes to capture.
- Evidence bundle: sample logs (~7 days of anonymized samples), a topology diagram, export manifest (sha256 checksums), and a short README describing retention and scrub rules.

2) Redaction defaults:
- We redact any token-like strings and full prompt/response payloads by default in the exported stream; we keep metrics, request IDs, latency, model.variant, and status codes.
- Customer may request expanded logs via an approval process (audit window).

3) Splunk HEC onramp (short checklist):
- Customer: create HEC endpoint inside VPC, enable TLS, provide HEC token via secure channel (KMS or pre-shared vault).
- Redwood: configure forwarder with HEC endpoint + token, set gzip compression on payloads, enable strict TLS cert validation.
- Optional: use private ALB + NLB for scale with health checks; we recommend 15s keepalive.

4) QRadar / syslog fallback:
- Provide RFC5424 mapping file (attached syslog-mapping-sample.txt). Use structured data fields for request_id and redaction marker.
- For QRadar, encourage using LEEF mapping or an ingestion lambda to convert to JSON for correlation.

5) Trace hooks (OTLP):
- Provide otlp-tracehook-snippets.md with examples for collector config (receiver: otlp; exporters: jaeger/splunk-otel-collector).
- Highlight tag policy: do not emit prompt/response text attributes; instead emit aggregates (token_count, latency_ms, model_name).

Attachments I'll include: acme-obsv-evidence-runbook-20261025.pdf, syslog-mapping-sample.txt, otlp-tracehook-snippets.md

I'll drop the runbook in Drive and mark the HubSpot ticket. LMK if you want me to call them directly.

kimberly

Hi Grace / Acme SecOps — thanks for the ask. Attached is a short runbook and three small artifacts that show the recommended config and evidence format. Summary below (one-page):

What Redwood will deliver for your private deployment:
- Syslog / HEC export: we can send structured RFC5424 syslog or push to Splunk HEC inside your VPC. We will not send prompt text by default — only telemetry, request ids, status codes, and model metadata.
- Tracing: runtime will emit OTLP spans to an OTEL collector sidecar (preferred) or to your collector endpoint. We'll supply collector snippets and a tracehook policy.
- Evidence bundle for audits: anonymized sample logs (7 days), topology diagram, and a signed manifest (sha256) listing files and hashes.

Action items / next steps:
1) Acme to confirm preferred collector pattern (sidecar vs central endpoint) and provide HEC endpoint + rotation method for token exchange.
2) Redwood to share runbook (attached) + sample syslog mapping (attached).
3) Schedule a 30-min technical handoff on Tue (we're proposing 10:00 AM PT).
